purpose: Independent simulated beginner mouse-only usability report, based only on visible session-5 interaction.
persona: Simulated first-time RILL beginner interested in a short hip-hop beat with a simple synth part.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: The empty-lane hint, instrument assignment, pencil instructions and Duplicate tool let me complete the task by mouse. Exact trimming needed a small correction.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark interface, teal waveforms and visible MIDI shapes look coherent and readable. Repeated clip names became abbreviated at the full-song zoom.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Drawing and duplicating clips responded quickly. Export displayed elapsed progress; native save dialogs briefly appeared black before rendering. This is a perceived session rating, not a performance benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Most controls had useful labels. The main uncertainties were locating exact pitches on sparsely labelled piano keys and trimming precisely at a zoomed-out scale.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The visible workflow covered audio, MIDI notes, a VST instrument, mouse naming, saving and both requested exports. I only evaluated a simple repeated arrangement and the supplied laboratory instrument.

findings.observation: Double-clicking the empty lane opened the Device library. Assign instrument created a MIDI lane visibly assigned to Rill Lab Sine.
The piano-roll Pencil tool said to drag to set length. Four mouse drags produced visible C4, D#4, G4 and F4 notes.
Before placing notes, most piano rows had no pitch labels. Labels on the newly drawn notes made the pitches clearer afterward.
Duplicate explained Click a clip to duplicate. Successive clicks placed the next audio and MIDI clips, and Fit brought the extended arrangement into view.
Dragging the last audio clip edge toward the 30-second ruler mark initially left the displayed duration at 30.134 seconds.
A second small edge drag changed the duration to exactly 30.000 seconds. The title duration supplied useful feedback.
File > Rename project exposed a Keyboard button. Clicking its on-screen keys and Apply name set NIGHT HOP without keyboard events.
After switching off Loop and clicking Play, the playhead advanced from bar 1 to bar 3 and both track meters were lit. Stop returned the transport to the beginning.
The native project and WAV save dialogs briefly appeared as black rectangles before their controls rendered in the next screenshot. They became usable without intervention.
The save picker proposed NIGHT HOP.rill in session-5. Clicking OK closed the picker and removed the unsaved dot beside the title.

WAV export showed Arrangement 0:30 and an Include effect tails checkbox. I unchecked tails. MIDI export showed Exported NIGHT HOP.mid, and Recent exports listed both NIGHT HOP.mid and NIGHT HOP.wav under Completed exports.

outcome.status: Completed in the visible UI: a named 30.000-second arrangement, project save accepted, MIDI success banner and both files listed as completed exports. File contents remain independently unverified.
outcome.composition: At 112 BPM in 4/4, the supplied Circuit rhythm audio was repeated across 14 bars, with the final audio copy trimmed to two bars. A four-note C4, D#4, G4, F4 MIDI motif was repeated in fourteen one-bar clips. This was intended as a simple hip-hop beat with a synth part; no sound or genre judgment was auditioned.
outcome.instrument: Rill Lab Sine, shown as VST3 in the library and assigned on the instrument lane.
outcome.playback_observed: Play changed to Pause; transport advanced from 001.01.00 to 003.01.00, the yellow playhead moved, and both track meters lit. No visible playback failure was observed. This does not establish heard audio.

limitations: No composition/project/file contents were inspected. Output paths come from visible save-dialog breadcrumbs and filenames; independent coordinator verification follows.
No audio capture was auditioned, so sound, balance, genre fit and audio quality were not verified.
The WAV success indication was its entry under Completed exports, not a separately observed WAV completion toast. The screenshot named 26-wav-success.png actually shows export still in progress.
Only the installed laboratory VST3 instrument was tested; this does not establish compatibility with other plug-ins.
Laboratory software graphics and virtual audio conditions apply. Elapsed interaction time includes tools and screenshots and is not a hardware latency or performance benchmark.
